en: Jose Rizal wrote his final poem, "Mi Ultimo Adios," secretly on the eve of his execution.
The Philippine eagle, locally called the monkey-eating eagle, is the country's official national bird.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the mountains of Ifugao by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago.
Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara co-invented the two-way television telephone, a precursor to modern video calls, in 1955.
The Malolos Constitution established the First Philippine Republic and was the first democratic constitution in Asia.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a traditional two-step forward dance.
The Mangyan people of Mindoro preserve their culture using an ancient pre-Hispanic writing system called Surat Mangyan.
Juan Luna painted the famous masterpiece "Spoliarium," which won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition.
Baybayin is an ancient Philippine writing system where each character represents a complete syllable rather than a single letter.
Emilio Aguinaldo officially proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The traditional Filipino value of "bayanihan" is visually demonstrated when an entire community helps carry a nipa hut.
The Philippine tarsier is a tiny primate famous for having enormous eyes that are larger than its brain.
